main_text.head: POst dictas terminorum comparationes, de rationum comparatione dicendum restat, ubi Proportio occurrit.
main_text.p: Euclides §d. 5 ἀναλογίαν definit, τῶν λόγων ὁμοιότητα, rationum similitudinem, Aristoteles lib. 5. cap. 3. Ethicorum, τῶν λόγων ἰσότητα, rationum æqualitatem. Quòd si & nos eam λόγων ταυτότητα, id est, rationum identitatem definiremus, ab Euclidis sententia nihil euariaremus, qui 6 d. 5 eodem modo loquitur, Proportionales quantitates appellans, eandem interse rationem obtinétes. Etsi uerò definitiones hæ proportioni Geometricæ, proprièe competant: tamen si Rationis uox latè accipiatur, pro respectu, generalis erit: ut quemadmodum ratio est mutuus duorum terminorum respectus, ita proportio similium inter se rationum habitudo.
main_text.head: Proportio uel est Arithmetica, uel Geometrica.

p.i: Græcè τωυτότης ὁμοφορᾶς, Vt in 8, 7, 6. Item 12, 9, 6, 3. Hic duæ sunt proportiones, in quarum utraq; æqualitas differentiarum, seu antecedentium æquus excessus cernitur: in priore differentia est 1, in posteriore 3. Sic in 15, 11 : 8, 4. Vt 15 superant 11 quaternario, ita 8 superat 4 eodem.

page.notes: The right-hand facing page is cut off at the edge; only fragments of its text are visible and are not transcribed. Greek and Hebrew copied as printed; some Greek letters in the scan are doubtful (the λόγων and ταυτότητα forms). The woodcut initial P is joined to the first word "Ost", printed as "Ost" with the initial P. The Greek phrase is printed in Greek letters and is copied as far as legible; the word after Arith- is a running catchword-like fragment and may be incomplete. Partial text at the right edge belongs to the adjacent page and is not transcribed.
